name: Chicken, mushroom & broccoli glass-noodle stir-fry (logged batch)

source.author: User's logged batch — cooked 2026-08-22
source.notes: Reference log of a batch the user actually cooked (exact amounts below). No oil or sauce was specified — assumed ~1 tbsp oil for stir-frying and light salt/pepper seasoning; sodium is low as-computed and rises if soy/salt is added. Tell me the oil/soy used and I'll adjust. Mushrooms ~150 g (8), onion ~75 g (½), zucchini ~400 g (2).

steps: Sear chicken strips, then stir-fry the veg and noodles together.

batch_totals.note: Sodium low as-computed (~600 mg batch) — rises with any added soy/salt.

him.verdict: A lean, high-protein cutting plate — 40 g protein for ~408 kcal (~9.8 g protein per 100 kcal) and only ~8 g fat/serving, with a big volume of veg and ~3 g fiber. Broccoli brings vitamin C + folate, mushrooms add selenium (a sperm micro). Low sodium AS COOKED here (no heavy sauce) — a plus versus the soy-loaded stir-fries. Glass noodles are the one refined carb, but they're well balanced by the protein and veg.
flags: 40 g protein/serving, very lean (~8 g fat)
suggested_mods: Add a handful of spinach for more folate + iron at almost no calories
If you season with soy, use low-sodium and go light — that's the only thing that would push sodium up

her_preconception.verdict: Strong for her too — broccoli folate + vitamin C, iron paired with that vitamin C for absorption, choline and selenium, all on lean protein with no safety flags (everything fully cooked, no sprouts, no high-mercury fish). Add greens to push the folate even higher.
prenatal_highlights: folate + vitamin C from broccoli (vitamin C also aids iron absorption)
suggested_mods: Toss in spinach for extra folate + iron
Keep it lightly seasoned to hold the sodium down

cooking_guide: Prep everything first — stir-fry moves fast. Soak the glass noodles in warm water until pliable (5-10 min), drain, and snip shorter with scissors.
Steam or blanch the broccoli ~2 min (it's the densest veg), then drain — this way it cooks evenly and stays bright and crisp-tender.
Pat the chicken strips dry and season lightly. Heat the pan/wok hot before the oil goes in — high heat sears, low heat steams.
Stir-fry the chicken in a single layer until just cooked, then remove (crowding makes it grey and watery).
Stir-fry the garlic and onion briefly, then the mushrooms — leave the mushrooms undisturbed a minute to brown (moving them too soon makes them release water and steam).
Add the zucchini and blanched broccoli and toss 2-3 min to keep them crisp-tender.
Return the chicken, add the noodles, and season to taste (salt/pepper, or a splash of low-sodium soy); toss 1-2 min to combine and heat through.
Serve promptly. Tip: a squeeze of lemon or lime at the end lifts the whole dish.
